top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is the only candidate-bearing proposal on the slate, and it matches my round-2 preference on the common literary criteria. His voice rests on language and imagery, not topicality. Formal ambition is carried across very large structures, as publicly described for Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid. Memory, the body, dream and cosmology recur as one coherent imaginative project, with poetry as the formative root of the prose. The citation scope is clean: one writer, one language, with prose as the load-bearing element and poetry named only as its root, since the poetry is thinly covered in translation. Reservations remain. I cannot judge Romanian rhythm, syntax and sonic patterning through translation. Whether the late long novels deepen the early project or partly repeat it is unresolved. The whole-oeuvre claim is only partly tested. All of this rests on public knowledge and the supplied descriptions, not independent verification or close reading. None of these reservations is strong enough to prefer no award (P000), which I rank last because the shortlist contains a writer whose case I judge to meet the criteria. Carson and Wright, my alternatives, are not on the slate as separate proposals.
